title: Generators, decorators, context managers
exp: These features distinguish idiomatic Python from basic Python. Generators are essential for large file processing.
pts: Generator: uses yield instead of return. Produces one value at a time without building the full list in memory.
Generator expression: (x*2 for x in items) -- lazy list comprehension.
Decorator: wraps another function to add behaviour. @functools.wraps preserves the wrapped function name.
@contextmanager: simplest way to write a custom context manager using yield.
*args and **kwargs: used in decorators to pass all arguments through.

viz.note: Generator: producer pauses at each yield, consumer processes, producer resumes. List: fully builds before consumer starts.

qa.q: What is a generator and why use one over a list?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A generator produces values one at a time on demand without computing all values upfront. Loading a 10GB CSV into a list crashes. A generator reads one batch at a time using constant memory regardless of file size. Use generators whenever processing data larger than available RAM.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Python interpreter executes bytecode under the CPython Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), managing objects via reference counting and cycle GC.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Attempting CPU-bound parallelism with Python threading fails due to GIL serialization; memory leaks occur from circular references.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Multiprocessing bypasses the GIL for CPU tasks at the cost of inter-process communication (IPC) serialization overhead.

qa.q: How does a context manager guarantee cleanup?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The code after yield in a @contextmanager always runs when the with block exits -- whether normally or via an exception. Use for file handles, database connections, threading locks -- anything that must be released even on error.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Python interpreter executes bytecode under the CPython Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), managing objects via reference counting and cycle GC.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Attempting CPU-bound parallelism with Python threading fails due to GIL serialization; memory leaks occur from circular references.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Multiprocessing bypasses the GIL for CPU tasks at the cost of inter-process communication (IPC) serialization overhead.
